steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan on medium heat and add the cumin; wait until it sizzles.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until they smell good.
Add the onion and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until soft and see-through.
Add the potato and green chilli, cover, and cook on low to medium for about 5 minutes, until the potato is half done.
Add the cauliflower and stir-fry on medium for 3 minutes, then mix in the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders and garam masala.
Add the salt and 2 to 3 spoons of water, cover, and cook on low for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until both are just soft.
Add the tomato and crushed kasuri methi and fry uncovered on medium-high for 2 to 4 minutes, until the tomato loses its raw smell.
Turn off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves on top and serve with roti.
note: This is the dry everyday version both sources cook; the cream, butter and bay leaf from the old restaurant-style recipe are gone. One source is far more generous with vegetables than the other, so the amounts sit between them at about 200 g of vegetables a person.
